newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Regional privatisation chief shot dead in Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: Regional privatisation chief shot dead in Ukraine.

text.p: The privatisation chief for Ukraine's Crimean peninsula was shot dead on his doorstep on Friday, a press spokesman for the prosecutor's office said.
"The state property fund head, Alexei Golovizin, was found...on his doorstep with three bullet wounds to the chest and head. He was taken to hospital where he died," spokesman Anatoly Titarchuk said.
He added that an investigation was under way but there were no immediate indications as to who was responsible for the murder.
Since January 1995 Golovizin, 58, had been in charge of the privatisation process which got going early last year after a three-year moratorium.

Crimea, Ukraine's autonomous region populated predominantly by ethnic Russians, has one of the highest crime rates in the country. Police figures show 369 murders were committed last year and 119 so far in 1997.
Last year a local administration chief and the head of the interior ministry department handling the fight against economic crimes were murdered.
